title: Thread-safe rate limiting
idea: A thread-safe rate limiter makes read-refill-check-spend one atomic step per key, so two threads can never both spend the last token.

analogy.text: One cookie left in a jar. Two hands reach in; whoever grabs it first takes it, and the other finds the jar empty.
analogy.breaks: Hands cannot overlap; threads can, unless a lock or CAS stops them.

points: Check-then-act on a shared count lets two threads pass on one token.
Separate atomic get and decrement still race; check and spend must be one step.
Lock per key, not per limiter, so no key waits on another key's lock.
In a `ConcurrentHashMap`, `computeIfAbsent` builds one bucket per key under contention.

messages.label: tokens?
messages.note: Unsafe version. Thread A reads one token left.

messages.label: tokens?
messages.note: Before A spends, Thread B reads the same single token.

messages.label: spend, allow
messages.note: A decrements and allows its request. Tokens are now zero.

messages.label: spend, allow
messages.note: B acts on its stale read. Two calls passed; tokens are now minus one.

messages.label: lock, check, spend
messages.note: Safe version. A holds the bucket lock while it checks and spends.

messages.label: lock (waits)
messages.note: B blocks on the same lock until A has finished.

messages.label: 0 tokens: reject
messages.note: B sees the true count and is rejected. Exactly one call passed.

code.title: Prove the race
code.caption: A barrier holds both threads between check and spend, so the race shows every run. Then two fixes.

walk.text: Race two threads for one token: unsafe, locked, and compare-and-set.
Each thread tries once; join both before reading the result.
Check, wait for the other thread to check too, then spend.
`synchronized` makes check and spend one step for this bucket.
Lock-free: write only if the value is still what you read.

code.title: Many threads, many keys
code.caption: Eight threads hammer two keys. Each key gets exactly its budget, and each bucket is built once.

walk.text: Capacity 100, refill 50 per second, with a manual clock shared by threads.
Run a storm at time 0, then another one second later.
Eight threads each send 500 calls, alternating k1 and k2.
Buckets live in a ConcurrentHashMap; a counter records how many get built.
`computeIfAbsent` runs the factory at most once per key.
Lock only this key's bucket, then refill. A clock step back adds nothing.
Check and spend inside the same lock.

pitfalls: Never `get` then `put` a new bucket; two threads may each create one.
Avoid one global lock; it serializes every key and caps throughput.
Do not hold a bucket lock while doing I/O, such as logging to a remote sink.

quiz.q: What does the first line of LimiterRace print?
options: It changes from run to run
quiz.why: The barrier makes both threads see one token before either spends. Both atomic decrements then run, leaving minus one.

takeaway: Refill, check and spend under one lock per key, never across keys.
